questions.q: In what year was Salesforce founded?
questions.explain: Salesforce was founded in 1999 by Marc Benioff, Parker Harris, Dave Moellenhoff, and Frank Dominguez.

questions.q: What did Salesforce's "No Software" pitch mean in practice?
options: A free, open-source CRM with no cost at all
A product with no actual software, only consulting services
CRM delivered entirely through a web browser, hosted by Salesforce, sold as a subscription — no installation or on-site hardware required
A CRM that only worked on a single company's own private servers
questions.explain: The pitch was against the installed-software norm of the time: no local installation, no hardware to maintain, no IT department needed just to start.

questions.q: What is SaaS, the model this lesson says Salesforce helped popularize?
options: A type of on-premises server installation
A hardware standard for data centers
Software as a Service — software delivered over the internet, hosted by the vendor, sold by subscription
questions.explain: SaaS is the delivery model Salesforce bet on in 1999, now the default way most business software is sold.

questions.q: What happened in 2007, according to this lesson?
options: Force.com launched, opening the underlying platform for building custom applications beyond CRM
Lightning Experience was introduced as the first Salesforce interface
questions.explain: Force.com, launched in 2007, formalized the platform/application split — the ability to build custom apps on Salesforce's underlying platform.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how did Salesforce build out several of its "clouds," such as Marketing and Commerce?
options: By exclusively building every product line from scratch in-house
By renaming its original CRM product multiple times
Partly through major acquisitions, such as ExactTarget and Demandware
questions.explain: The lesson names ExactTarget (marketing), Demandware (commerce), Tableau (analytics), and Slack (collaboration) as acquisitions that grew Salesforce's product lines.
